properties.name: The agent establishes what KIND of thing is being designed, in the user's own domain language, before it captures the parts — and never by asking the user to pick node types
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, from Alex's first-run report on a real work project.

ALEX'S EXPERIENCE: *"It was a little unsure of how to store the data models for my project in the graph. It asked me what node types it should store them as. I didn't really know for sure so I told it to figure it out. It worked, but that might be confusing for someone who isn't technical… it should probably ask probing questions to figure this out without exposing internal components of the graph structure to the user."*

ANTHONY'S FRAMING: *"this gets at that reflow2 claims to 'design anything', whether that be an IT system of systems that includes a 'data model' OR a physical 'shop' that my brother wants to design that will generate blueprints and architectural drawings (structural, electrical, plumbing, etc) as artifacts in the graph. I think this point is already clear in reflow2, but I think we need to sharpen the agent's questions so that the right graph and artifacts can be generated… we do need to follow this in principle that the agent asks or determines appropriate systems engineering models for the design so that the design entities/components can properly be captured."*

WHAT IS REQUIRED:

1. **THE AGENT ESTABLISHES WHAT KIND OF THING IS BEING DESIGNED BEFORE IT CAPTURES THE PARTS.** A data model, a machine shop, a beamline and a process are not the same kind of object, and the entities worth capturing differ accordingly. This is a question the agent ASKS OR DETERMINES — not one it silently assumes and not one it skips.

2. **IT IS ASKED IN THE USER'S OWN DOMAIN LANGUAGE.** Probing questions about the thing — what it must do, what it is made of, what meets what, what would count as finished — never a request that the user choose a node type. **The mapping from their words to the schema is the agent's job**, which `capture-intent` already states and `describe_schema` already equips it for. Handing that question back is the inversion Alex hit, and it is the one behaviour this requirement forbids outright.

3. **THE ANSWER SHAPES EXTRACTION AND PHRASING, AND NEVER GATES COMPUTATION.** What kind of system it is may determine which questions get asked, which vocabulary the agent speaks back, and which artifacts are expected (blueprints, structural/electrical/plumbing drawings for a shop; schemas and migrations for an IT system). **It must never determine which analyses reflow2 will run.** A cycle detector runs wherever there are dependency edges, whoever calls them interfaces or interactions.

⭐ THE PRIOR ART, AND WHY ONLY HALF OF IT SURVIVES. reflow's `00b-framework_selection` / S-01A holds two separable things, and reflow2 dropped both together:
  · **THE TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY** (`definitions/framework_registry.json`) maps node → `service` / `gene` / `agent` / `species` and edge → `interface` / `interaction` / `relationship` over one universal graph. **Correctly rejected** by `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (now `dropped`): renaming the same structure changes nothing computable, adds a translation layer that can drift, and its load-bearing claim — *"framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available"* — makes capability conditional on a self-declared label, which is how a user gets a wrong answer for a reason they cannot see.
  · **THE SEMANTIC-MATCHING INTERVIEW** is a different thing and was not cosmetic. S-01A's rationale: *"Framework selection is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, not a configuration choice. Wrong framework = wrong insights."* LESSON-04: *"Framework abstractions must match system semantics. Workflows are state machines (not services), even though both could be 'engineered systems'. Wrong abstraction = wrong insights."* Its first action is *"Ask user to describe the system"* — **domain language, not node types.** THAT is what survives, and it is what this requirement asks for.

🛑 **THE DROPPED REQUIREMENT PREDICTED THIS AND NOBODY BUILT THE PART IT SAVED.** `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` closes by naming the middle path in as many words: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services') and discards the part that would make analyses conditional on a label."* It was dropped as a REGISTRY, its surviving half was written down, and the second user then hit exactly that gap. **This requirement is that middle path, raised by a user rather than by a re-reading.**

📌 RELATED AND NOT DUPLICATED: `req:defaults-do-not-assert` carries LESSON-01's real content (*do not default to UAF*) and forbids assuming the answer; this requires that the question be ASKED. `req:design-anything` establishes that the vocabulary is neutral; this is about the interview that makes a neutral vocabulary usable by someone who does not know it. `dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-project-that-is-not-software` records that the DELIVERY is still software-shaped, which is the same gap seen from the documentation side.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT BEING ASKED FOR: a framework registry, a catalogue of systems-engineering models inside reflow2, or a `Project.domain` value that switches behaviour. `Project.domain` today is written by genesis and read by nothing; whether this requirement is what should finally read it — and whether it must therefore become an enum rather than free text — is deliberately left open here.
